text: Dès le début, Viktor Quinlan a mis Kingsmoor FC sur de bons rails avec un penalty transformé à la 8ème minute, une occasion qui se marque presque 8 fois sur 10 (xG 0.76) [#152]. Il a rapidement doublé la mise à la 12ème minute, d'une belle action collective sur 8 passes [#222]. Mais Westport Albion a riposté avec deux buts rapides de Rafael Delacroix, surtout le second à bout portant qui valait presque un but sûr (xG 0.99) [#553]. Kenji Rahman a égalisé ensuite à la 51ème, assurant l'intensité de cette rencontre riche en occasions [#983]. Malgré un joueur en moins à la 81ème suite à un carton rouge, Kingsmoor a arraché un troisième but juste après, grâce à Luca Iversen sur un joli centre [#1495][#1516]. Les deux équipes ont montré un grand spectacle avec beaucoup d’attaques et un style ouvert, terminant sur un score nul de 3-3 passionnant [#152][#222][#401][#553][#983][#1516].

- Viktor Quinlan scored twice for Kingsmoor FC early on, including a penalty at 8' with xG 0.76, and an open play goal at 12' with xG 0.197 [#152, #222].
- Rafael Delacroix equalized for Westport Albion with two goals at 22' (xG 0.797) and 30' (xG 0.992) [#401, #553].
- Kenji Rahman leveled the match at 51' for Westport Albion with a goal xG 0.449 [#983].
- Felix Barros of Kingsmoor FC received a second yellow card and was sent off at 81' when Kingsmoor was trailing 2-3 [#1495].
- Luca Iversen scored for Kingsmoor FC at 82', with an xG of 0.854, keeping the match tied at 3-3 [#1516].

- Kingsmoor FC's first goal came from a penalty converted by Viktor Quinlan after the team was trailing, indicating a pressing success leading to a foul in the box. Their 4-4-2 wide crossing style suggests that their setup creates wide attacks but also sustains pressure in the final third to win penalties early [#152].
- Quinlan's second goal at 12' originated from an 8-pass build-up lasting 26.7 seconds, starting from a regain and involving multiple midfielders and wide players, showcasing Kingsmoor’s pattern of controlled possession and wide play culminating in a medium-assist finish—reflecting their 4-4-2 wide-crossing formation [#222].
- Westport Albion, also playing 4-4-2 but with a direct, vertical passing style, scored their first goal at 22' following a 7-pass build-up started from a regain, emphasizing quick ball progression and verticality to create a high xG chance at close range, consistent with their tactical style [#401].
- The equalizing goals for Westport at 30' and 51', both arising from open play, featured crosses and short assists in structured passing sequences, showing they balanced direct vertical passing with effective use of wide crosses, matching their 4-4-2 formation but adapting crossing to exploit wide areas [#553][#983].
- Kingsmoor's tactical change at 65', increasing pressing intensity, directness, and line height while chasing the game, indicates a shift to a higher, more aggressive style to regain control and create quicker attacking transitions, highlighting the tactical flexibility within their 4-4-2 wide system [#1187].
- Westport Albion’s adjustment at 79' to drop deeper and slow tempo, reducing press and line height, was a strategy to protect the lead defensively by sitting back, which aligns with their direct style by minimizing risk but inviting pressure [#1459].
- The late goal for Kingsmoor at 82' from a cross by Mason Morales and a quick 2-pass move after a regain illustrates Kingsmoor’s reliance on wide, crossing play to create quick, high-quality chances especially when behind, reinforcing their wide 4-4-2 approach [#1516].
- The red card for Kingsmoor's Felix Barros at 81' reduced their manpower, likely putting more pressure on their crossing and high press style during the game’s closing stages [#1494].
